section3.title: 3. Frequently Asked Questions on PPE Certification

item1.q: What is the difference between OSHA regulations and ANSI standards?
item1.a: OSHA sets the mandatory legal safety requirements for workplaces, while ANSI creates the performance and testing consensus standards for PPE that OSHA often adopts by reference.

item2.q: Can I use CE (European) certified PPE in US workplaces?
item2.a: Not automatically. PPE used in US workplaces must meet the specific ANSI, ASTM, or NIOSH standards required by OSHA, regardless of foreign certifications.

item3.a: While the PPE itself may have a manufacturer's lifespan or expiration date (especially hard hats and harnesses), employers must also ensure the PPE meets the current applicable consensus standard if regulations update.

item4.q: How do I verify certified PPE?
item4.a: Look for the specific ANSI standard marking (e.g., Z87.1 for eyewear) or NIOSH approval labels (e.g., TC numbers for respirators) stamped directly on the equipment or its packaging.
